editorial:
Imagine living in a tiny town tucked away in the mountains where a strange rule controls your entire life. In this village, only the first-born sons get to marry and have kids. Everyone else is basically stuck on the sidelines, watching their older brothers take all the happiness. You will find yourself rooting for the younger brothers as they try to find ways around these old laws. It is a mix of funny moments and sad situations that shows how far people will go when they are desperate for love and a family of their own.

The acting is great because the characters feel like real people you might know, making the drama feel personal. While the pace starts a bit slow, the way the stories overlap keeps you interested. If you enjoy movies that poke fun at silly traditions while still making you feel for the characters, you will love this. You should definitely try to find the 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection for the best picture quality, or see if you can rent it on Apple TV for a cozy movie night with friends.
endingExplained: The movie ends with a bittersweet look at the village laws. Some characters try to cheat the system to get married, but the pressure of the community is too strong. You see that while some find small ways to be happy, the cycle of the first-born son rule continues. It wraps up by showing that tradition often wins over individual happiness, leaving the younger brothers in a tough spot.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves human stories and quirky old movies.
